```{r}
data <- read.csv("SENIC.csv")
str(data)
SENIC_orig <- data[,c("stay","inf","census","nurses")]

#Missing Values  
sum(!complete.cases(SENIC_orig))

str(SENIC_orig)

summary(SENIC_orig)
```

#Determine Outliers or potential influential data
```{r}
#stay
Q1 <- quantile(SENIC_orig$stay,0.25)
Q3 <- quantile(SENIC_orig$stay,0.75)
IQR_val <- IQR(SENIC_orig$stay)

LB <- Q1- 1.5*IQR_val
UB <- Q3+ 1.5*IQR_val

SENIC_orig[SENIC_orig$stay < LB | SENIC_orig$stay > UB,]
```

#Remove Outliers
```{r}

scatterplotMatrix(SENIC_orig, smooth = F, regLine=T, main="With Outliers")

#stay response variable is positive and skewed to the right

SENIC.no.outliers <- SENIC_orig[-c(47,112),]

scatterplotMatrix(SENIC.no.outliers, smooth = F, regLine=T, main="No Outliers")

summary(SENIC.no.outliers)

```
#EDA
#Based on scatter plots:
#Positive but weak relationship. That is, as the variables inf, census, and nurses increase, the length of stay also increases
#The distribution of stay, census, and nurses are positive and rightly skewed while inf resembles a bell shaped curve with high peakness. This means that most of the data fall on the smaller values.
#The estimated PDF of the response variable 'stay' seems to resemble a Gamma or inverse gaussian distribution because of right skewness
#census and nurses have strong and positive correlation (+0.9)


#Fit an OLS regression model using all variables

```{r}
SENIC.lm <- lm(stay ~ inf + census + nurses, data=SENIC_orig)
summary(SENIC.lm)

#Magnitude of the error (Fox, 2016 p. 307)
fitted_vals <- fitted(SENIC.lm)

groups <- cut(fitted_vals,
              breaks = quantile(fitted_vals, probs = seq(0,1,0.25)),
              include.lowest = TRUE)

sd_by_group <- tapply(resid(SENIC.lm), groups, sd)

sd_by_group

max(sd_by_group, na.rm = TRUE) / min(sd_by_group, na.rm = TRUE)
```
#Linear Model Diagnostics: Unusual and Influential Data

#Leverage
```{r}
plot(SENIC.lm, which=5)
```


#Detecting Outliers
```{r}
#Studentized residuals

ols_plot_resid_stud(SENIC.lm)

#Bonferroni Adjustment
outlierTest(SENIC.lm) #based on studentized residuals
```



#Measuring Influence
#the observations that have major influence in the regression coefficients are 47 and 112 (Cook's distance)
#the observations that have major influence in the regression coefficients are 47 and 112 (DFFITS and DFBETAS)
#the observation that decrease the precision of estimation is 47 (COVRATIO)
```{r}

#Influence of regression coefficients
ols_plot_cooksd_chart(SENIC.lm)
ols_plot_dfbetas(SENIC.lm)
ols_plot_dffits(SENIC.lm)

#Influence on standard errors
covr <- covratio(SENIC.lm)

n <- length(covr)
p <- length(coef(SENIC.lm)) - 1
threshold <- 3*(p+1)/n

plot(covr,
     ylab="COVRATIO",
     main="COVRATIO Plot")

abline(h=1, col="red")
abline(h=c(1-threshold, 1+threshold),
       col="blue", lty=2)

inf_points <- which(abs(covr - 1) > threshold)

text(inf_points,
     covr[inf_points],
     labels=inf_points,
     pos=3,
     col="blue")
```

#Check whether the assumptions of OLS regression model are satisfied by the data set.Focus on normality and homoskedasticity assumptions.

```{r}
#Model Diagnostics

#par(mfrow=c(4,1))
plot(SENIC.lm)

#first graph (Residuals vs Fitted): the errors seem to be scattered uniformly across the fitted values, suggesting homoscedasticity

## Score Test for Non-Constant Error Variance (Breusch-Pagan test)
#H0: error variance does not change with the level of the response (fitted values)
#Ha: error variance changes with the level of the response (fitted values), or with a linear combination of predictors)
#Reject H0; model is heteroscedastic
ncvTest(SENIC.lm)

crPlots(SENIC.lm)
ceresPlots(SENIC.lm)

## testing for independence of error terms ----
durbinWatsonTest(SENIC.lm)

## testing for normality of error terms ----
shapiro.test(SENIC.lm$residuals)

## other data considerations ----
### checking for multicollinearity ----
vif(SENIC.lm)
sqrt(vif(SENIC.lm)) > 2 # problem?

### identify possible outliers ----
outlierTest(SENIC.lm) # based on studentized residuals


#Without Outliers
SENIC.lm.no.outliers <- lm(stay ~ inf + census + nurses, data=SENIC.no.outliers)
plot(SENIC.lm.no.outliers)
crPlots(SENIC.lm.no.outliers)
ceresPlots(SENIC.lm.no.outliers)

```

#Give the value of an appropriate measure to evaluate the performance of this model.

```{r}
summary_R_IC_GCV <- function(models, cv.model=SENIC){
  
  n <- length(models)
  Adjusted_R <- numeric(n)
  cv.error <- numeric(n)
  aic <- numeric(n)
  bic <- numeric(n)
  
  for(i in 1:n){
  #R^2
    deviance <- summary(models[[i]])$deviance
    null_deviance <- summary(models[[i]])$null.deviance
    Adjusted_R[i] <- 1 - (deviance / null_deviance)
  
  #CV MSPE
    set.seed(100)
  cv.error[i] = cv.glm(cv.model , models[[i]] ,K=10)$delta[1]
  
  #AIC
  aic[i] = AIC(models[[i]])
  
  #BIC
  bic[i] = BIC(models[[i]])
  }
  
  df <- data.frame(
    Model = names(models),
    Rsquared = round(as.numeric(Adjusted_R),4),
    CV_MSPE = round(cv.error,4),
    AIC= aic,
    BIC=bic
    
  )
  return(df)
}

summary_R_IC_GCV2 <- function(models, cv.model=SENIC){
  
  n <- length(models)
  Adjusted_R <- numeric(n)
  cv.error <- numeric(n)
  aic <- numeric(n)
  bic <- numeric(n)
  
  for(i in 1:n){
  #R^2
   # r <- pscl::pR2(models[[i]])
    #Adjusted_R[i] <- r["McFadden"]
  
  #CV MSPE
    set.seed(100)
  cv.error[i] = cv.glm(cv.model , models[[i]] ,K=10)$delta[1]
  
  #AIC
  aic[i] = AIC(models[[i]])
  
  #BIC
  bic[i] = BIC(models[[i]])
  }
  
  df <- data.frame(
    Model = names(models),
    #Rsquared = round(as.numeric(Adjusted_R),4),
    CV_MSPE = round(cv.error,4),
    AIC= aic,
    BIC=bic
    
  )
  return(df)
}
```

#Evaluate the predictive ability of the model by randomly selecting ∼ 80% of the dataset to be used as training data and the rest of the observations as test data. Output necessary measures.


```{r}
evaluate_models <- function(models, test_data, response_var){
  
  bias <- function(y, yhat){
    mean(yhat - y)
  }
  
  norm_bias <- function(y, yhat){
    mean(yhat - y) / mean(y)
  }
  
  mspe <- function(y, yhat){
    mean((yhat - y)^2)
  }
  
  #mspe <- function(y, yhat){
   # mean(((yhat - y)/y)^2)
  #}
  
  #rmse <- function(y, yhat){
    #sqrt(mse(y, yhat))
  #}
  
  rmspe <- function(y, yhat){
    sqrt(mspe(y, yhat))
  }
  
  nrmse <- function(y, yhat){
    rmse(y, yhat) / (max(y) - min(y))
  }
  
  mae <- function(y, yhat){
    mean(abs(yhat - y))
  }
  
  mape <- function(y, yhat){
    mean(abs((yhat - y)/y)) * 100
  }
  
  smape <- function(y, yhat){
    mean(2 * abs(yhat - y) / (abs(y) + abs(yhat))) * 100
  }
  
  
  y <- test_data[[response_var]]
  
  results <- lapply(names(models), function(name){
    
    model <- models[[name]]
    
    #Get predictions
    yhat <- predict(model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
    
    data.frame(
      Model = name,
      Bias = bias(y, yhat),
      Normalized_Bias = norm_bias(y, yhat),
      #MSE = mse(y, yhat),
      MSPE = mspe(y, yhat),
      NRMSE = nrmse(y, yhat),
      #RMSE = rmse(y, yhat),
      RMSPE = rmspe(y, yhat),
      MAE = mae(y, yhat),
      MAPE = mape(y, yhat),
      SMAPE = smape(y, yhat)
    )
  })
  
  final <- do.call(rbind, results)
final[ , -1] <- round(final[ , -1], 4) #round to 4 decimal places
final
}
```

```{r}
summarize_model.fit <- function(model_list){
  
  n <- length(model_list)
  P_value <- numeric(n)
  
  for(i in 1:n){
    
    if(i %% 2 != 0 && i < n){
      P_value[i] <- anova(model_list[[i]], model_list[[i+1]], test="F")$'Pr(>F)'[2]
    } else {
      P_value[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  data_frame <- data.frame(
    Model = c("stay ~ inf","stay ~ ns(inf)",
              "stay ~ census","stay ~ ns(census)",
              "stay ~ nurses","stay ~ ns(nurses)"),
    P_value_anova = round(P_value,4)
  )
  
  return(data_frame)
}
  
  
 summarize_model.fit(model_list)
```

#Determine if using a GAM improved prediction accuracy compared to the linear model by considering the same train and test data set used in Item 1e. For this, choose the best fit among items 2b, 2c, 2d to model the chosen variable in 2a and consider a linear fit for the remaining variables.


```{r}

train_data2 <- train_data_updated
test_data2 <- test_data_updated

#best fit among items 2b, 2c, 2d

#2b
model.2b=glm(stay ~ poly(census,5),data=train_data2)

#Define breaks from the TRAIN data
interval  <- 9
by        <- floor((max(train_data2$census) - min(train_data2$census)) / interval)
breaks_n  <- seq(from = min(train_data2$census),
                 to   = max(train_data2$census),
                 by   = by)

interval2 <- 4
by2        <- floor((max(train_data2$census) - min(train_data2$census)) / interval2)
breaks_n2  <- seq(from = min(train_data2$census),
                 to   = max(train_data2$census),
                 by   = by2)

# ensure the upper endpoint is included
if (tail(breaks_n, 1) < max(train_data2$census)){
  breaks_n <- c(breaks_n, max(train_data2$census))
}

if (tail(breaks_n2, 1) < max(train_data2$census)){
  breaks_n2 <- c(breaks_n2, max(train_data2$census))
}

# 2) Create a factor column in BOTH sets, using the SAME breaks
train_data2$census_grp <- cut(train_data2$census, breaks=breaks_n, include.lowest=TRUE, right=TRUE)
test_data2$census_grp  <- cut(test_data2$census,  breaks=breaks_n, include.lowest=TRUE, right=TRUE)

train_data2$census_grp2 <- cut(train_data2$census, breaks=breaks_n2, include.lowest=TRUE, right=TRUE)
test_data2$census_grp2  <- cut(test_data2$census,  breaks=breaks_n2, include.lowest=TRUE, right=TRUE)

# 3) Fit your “2c” and downstream models using census_grp (no inline cut() in the formula)
model.2c1 <- lm(stay ~ census_grp, data = train_data2)



model.2c2 <- lm(stay ~ census_grp2*poly(census, 5, raw = TRUE), data = train_data2)

# 2b and 2d
model.2d1 <- glm(stay ~ splines::bs(census, df=6), data=train_data2)
model.2d2 <- glm(stay ~ splines::ns(census, df=9), data=train_data2)

models_2 <- list(
  'glm(stay ~ poly(census,5))'                       = model.2b,
  'lm(stay ~ census_grp) [constant step]'                             = model.2c1,
  'lm(stay ~ census_grp * poly(census,2,raw=TRUE)) [piecewise polynomial]'   = model.2c2,
  'glm(stay ~ bs(census,df=6))'                       = model.2d1,
  'glm(stay ~ ns(census,df=9))'                       = model.2d2
)


evaluate_models(models_2, test_data2, "stay")  #the _____ model has the best predictive capability

#Full model

models111 <- list(
  'glm(stay ~ poly(census,5))'                       = model2b_full,
  'lm(stay ~ census_grp) [constant step]'           = model2c1_full,
  'lm(stay ~ census_grp * poly(census,2,raw=TRUE)) [piecewise polynomial]'   = model2c2_full,
  'glm(stay ~ bs(census,df=6))'                       = model2d1_full,
  'glm(stay ~ ns(census,df=9))'                       = model2d2_full
)

df_AIC_BIC <- data.frame(
  Model= c( 'glm(stay ~ poly(census,5))', 'lm(stay ~ census_grp) [constant step]','lm(stay ~ census_grp * poly(census,4,raw=TRUE)) [piecewise polynomial]', 'glm(stay ~ bs(census,df=6))', 'glm(stay ~ ns(census,df=9))'),
  AIC=AIC(model2b_full,model2c1_full,model2c2_full,model2d1_full,model2d2_full),
  BIC=BIC(model2b_full,model2c1_full,model2c2_full,model2d1_full,model2d2_full)
)
df_AIC_BIC

library(mgcv)
model_gam <- mgcv::gam(stay ~ inf + nurses + splines::bs(census, df=3), data = train_data2, family = inverse.gaussian(link = "1/mu^2"))

models_3 <- list(
  'GAM: stay ~ inf + nurses + bs(census, df=6) [Inverse Gaussian]'                = model_gam,
  'GLM: stay ~ inf + census + nurses [Inverse Gaussian] UPDATED' = SENIC.glm.invgaussian_updated.train
)

#Predictive Ability
evaluate_models(models_3, test_data2, "stay")

#Consider full model
model_gam_full <- mgcv::gam(stay ~ inf + nurses + splines::bs(census, df=3), data = SENIC.no.outliers, family = inverse.gaussian(link = "1/mu^2"))

models0000 <- list(

)

summary_R_IC_GCV2(models0000, cv.model = SENIC.no.outliers)[,c(1,3:4)]
```
